learning_activity_name: Describe the classification of computer architecture (Von Neumann and Non Von Neumann, Harvard Architecture, Modified Harvard Architecture, Flynn’s Taxonomy)
sla_name: Classification of computer architecture
sla_assessment_criteria: The classification of computer architecture is properly described.
sla_teaching_aids: Simulators (Celiot|Celiot++|Jeliot|Etc)|Computer system|Modals|Video tutorials|Internet resources|Marker pens|Flip charts|Non- Visual Desktop Access (NVDA)|Virtual Reality (VR)/Augmented Reality (AR) tools|Security Operations Center (SOC) Simulator|Simulator creation tools (TopGen|Grey box|TopoMojo|VTunnel
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Computer architecture describes how the processor, memory and input-output units are organised and how instructions and data move between them. Architectures are classified by how they store programs and data and by how many instruction and data streams they handle.
sla_notes_details: The Von Neumann architecture stores instructions and data in the same memory and uses one bus, so the CPU cannot fetch an instruction and data at the same time (the Von Neumann bottleneck). The Harvard architecture uses separate memories and buses for instructions and data, allowing both to be accessed simultaneously. The Modified Harvard architecture keeps separate caches for instructions and data but one main memory, which is the design used in most modern processors. Non-Von Neumann designs include dataflow and parallel machines. Flynn's taxonomy classifies machines by instruction and data streams: SISD (single instruction, single data), SIMD (single instruction, multiple data, as in GPUs), MISD and MIMD (multiple instructions, multiple data, as in multicore processors and clusters).
sla_notes_illustrations: A microcontroller in a washing machine is often a pure Harvard design with the program in flash memory and data in RAM, while a smartphone processor is a modified Harvard multicore MIMD system that also uses SIMD units for image processing.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing the classification helps a buyer or technician understand why a multicore phone runs many apps at once and why a graphics card is fast at video and games.
sla_exercise: State one difference between Von Neumann and Harvard architectures.::Von Neumann uses one memory for instructions and data, while Harvard uses separate memories and buses for them.||What does SIMD stand for and where is it used?::Single Instruction Multiple Data; it is used in graphics processors and multimedia processing.||Which Flynn class describes a multicore processor?::MIMD (multiple instruction, multiple data).

learning_activity_name: Demonstrate understanding of Boolean algebra and logic gates (Logic expressions, standard logic gate symbols, logic circuits)
sla_name: Boolean algebra and logic gates
sla_assessment_criteria: Understanding of Boolean algebra and logic gates is correctly demonstrated.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Boolean algebra is the mathematics of two-valued variables (0 and 1, false and true) used to describe and simplify digital circuits. Logic gates are the electronic building blocks that implement Boolean operations.
sla_notes_details: The basic operations are AND (output 1 only when all inputs are 1), OR (output 1 when at least one input is 1) and NOT (inverts the input). Derived gates are NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR; NAND and NOR are universal gates because any circuit can be built from either one. Standard laws include commutative, associative, distributive, identity, complement, idempotent, absorption and De Morgan's laws: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B and NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B. A logic expression is converted to a truth table, simplified (algebraically or with Karnaugh maps) and drawn as a logic circuit using the standard gate symbols.
sla_notes_illustrations: Simplify X = A.B + A.B' : X = A.(B + B') = A.1 = A. The circuit that needed two AND gates, one NOT gate and one OR gate is reduced to a plain wire from A.
sla_notes_daily_life: Alarm systems use logic circuits: an alarm rings when the door sensor is triggered AND the system is armed, which is a simple AND gate.
sla_exercise: State De Morgan's first law.::NOT(A AND B) equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B).||Give the output of an XOR gate when both inputs are 1.::0, because XOR gives 1 only when the inputs are different.||Simplify A + A.B.::A, by the absorption law: A + A.B = A.(1 + B) = A.

learning_activity_name: Explore computer memory (Meaning, design principles, memory hierarchy and interfacing, cache memory, memory mapping, primary & secondary memory)
sla_name: Computer memory and memory hierarchy
sla_method: Simulation/ virtual lab/ Tutorial videos/ Case studies
sla_assessment_criteria: Computer memory is properly explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Computer memory is the component that stores programs and data that the processor uses. Memory is organised in a hierarchy so that the computer gets both speed and large capacity at an affordable cost.
sla_notes_details: The hierarchy from fastest and smallest to slowest and largest is: CPU registers, cache memory (L1, L2, L3), main memory (RAM), and secondary storage (SSD, hard disk, optical and tape). Primary memory (RAM and ROM) is directly accessed by the CPU, while secondary memory is non-volatile and accessed through input-output channels. Cache memory holds copies of frequently used data and works because of locality of reference (temporal and spatial). Memory mapping decides where a block of main memory is placed in the cache: direct mapping, associative mapping and set-associative mapping. Design principles include speed, capacity, cost per bit, volatility and interfacing with the address, data and control buses through decoders and memory controllers.
sla_notes_illustrations: If a program requests data found in cache the access is a hit and takes a few nanoseconds; if it is not found it is a miss and the block is fetched from RAM. With a hit rate of 95 percent, most accesses are fast even though the cache is small.
sla_notes_daily_life: A phone with more RAM keeps more apps open without reloading, and an SSD makes a laptop start faster than a hard disk because it is a faster level of the hierarchy.
sla_exercise: Name two levels of the memory hierarchy faster than RAM.::CPU registers and cache memory.||What is a cache hit?::When the data requested by the CPU is found in the cache.||Name one cache mapping technique.::Direct mapping (or associative or set-associative mapping).

learning_activity_name: Analyse instruction set architecture (Instruction set types, registers, instruction execution cycles, addressing modes, register transfer language, ARM and x86 architectures)
sla_name: Instruction set architecture
sla_assessment_criteria: Instruction set architecture is correctly analysed.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The instruction set architecture (ISA) is the interface between hardware and software; it defines the instructions a processor can execute, its registers, data types and addressing modes.
sla_notes_details: Instruction set types include data transfer, arithmetic and logic, control (branch and jump) and input-output instructions. ISAs are grouped as RISC (reduced instruction set computers, such as ARM, with simple fixed-length instructions) and CISC (complex instruction set computers, such as x86, with variable-length and powerful instructions). Instruction execution follows the fetch, decode, execute and store cycle, controlled by the program counter and instruction register. Addressing modes tell the CPU how to find an operand: immediate, direct, indirect, register, register indirect and indexed. Register transfer language (RTL) describes micro-operations symbolically, for example R1 <- R2 + R3 or MAR <- PC.
sla_notes_illustrations: For the instruction ADD R1, R2, R3 the CPU fetches it from the address in PC, decodes it, the ALU adds R2 and R3, and the result is stored in R1 while PC is incremented to the next instruction.
sla_notes_daily_life: Most smartphones use ARM processors because they are power efficient, while most desktop and laptop computers use x86 processors for high performance.
sla_exercise: Name the four stages of the instruction cycle.::Fetch, decode, execute and store (write back).||Give one example each of a RISC and a CISC architecture.::ARM is RISC and x86 is CISC.||What is immediate addressing?::A mode in which the operand is part of the instruction itself.

learning_activity_name: Describe I/O system (Direct Memory Access, Interrupt and exception, privileged / non privileged instruction)
sla_name: Input-output system, DMA and interrupts
sla_assessment_criteria: I/O system is properly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The input-output (I/O) system connects the processor and memory to peripheral devices. It manages data transfer between devices that work at very different speeds.
sla_notes_details: Data transfer can be by programmed I/O (the CPU polls the device), interrupt-driven I/O (the device signals the CPU when ready) or Direct Memory Access (DMA), where a DMA controller moves blocks of data between device and memory without CPU involvement, and interrupts the CPU only at the end. An interrupt is a signal that causes the CPU to suspend its current program, save its state, run an interrupt service routine and then resume. An exception is a synchronous event caused by the running instruction, such as division by zero or an invalid address. Privileged instructions (changing memory protection, halting, I/O access) can be executed only in kernel mode, while non-privileged instructions can run in user mode; this protects the system from faulty programs.
sla_notes_illustrations: When a file is copied from a flash disk, the DMA controller transfers the data blocks into RAM and raises one interrupt when done, so the processor is free to run other programs during the copy.
sla_notes_daily_life: Pressing a key on a keyboard causes an interrupt so the computer responds immediately instead of continually checking the keyboard.
sla_exercise: What is the advantage of DMA?::It transfers data between I/O devices and memory without occupying the CPU.||Differentiate an interrupt from an exception.::An interrupt is caused by an external device event, while an exception is caused by the instruction being executed, such as division by zero.||Why are some instructions privileged?::To prevent user programs from directly controlling hardware and to protect the operating system.

learning_activity_name: Demonstrate function of memory and input-output system
sla_name: Functions of memory and input-output system
sla_assessment_criteria: Function of memory and input-output system is correctly demonstrated.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Memory and the I/O system work together to supply the processor with instructions and data and to send results to users. This activity demonstrates their operation using simulation.
sla_notes_details: Memory functions include storing instructions and data, providing fast access through address, data and control lines, and read and write operations controlled by the memory controller. The I/O system functions include device addressing (memory-mapped or port-mapped I/O), buffering to match device speeds, status reporting, error handling and data conversion. Using a simulator learners load a small program, watch the address bus select a memory location, see data placed on the data bus and observe how an I/O module signals when a device is ready. They record clock cycles for memory reads, writes and I/O transfers.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a simulator, a read operation places address 0010 on the address bus, activates the read line, and the value stored at 0010 appears on the data bus and is loaded into a register.
sla_notes_daily_life: When you save a document, the CPU writes data to memory and then the I/O system sends it to the disk, showing how memory and I/O cooperate.
sla_exercise: What is the function of the address bus during a memory read?::It carries the address of the memory location to be read.||Why is buffering needed in an I/O system?::To match the speed of slow devices with the fast processor.||Distinguish memory-mapped I/O from port-mapped I/O.::Memory-mapped I/O uses the same address space as memory, while port-mapped I/O uses a separate address space and special instructions.

learning_activity_name: Develop understanding of pipelining (Basics, types, stalling & forwarding, throughput and speedup, hazards) and Instruction Level Parallelism ( concept, compilation techniques, scalar versus superscalar pipelining, branch prediction, register renaming) and thread and data level parallelism
sla_name: Pipelining and instruction level parallelism
sla_assessment_criteria: Understanding of the pipelining, Instruction Level Parallelism, and thread and data level parallelism is correctly developed.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pipelining is a technique that overlaps the execution of several instructions so that different stages of different instructions are processed at the same time. It increases instruction throughput without increasing clock speed.
sla_notes_details: A classic pipeline has five stages: instruction fetch, decode, execute, memory access and write back. Speedup for k stages and n instructions is approximately (n x k) divided by (k + n - 1), approaching k for large n. Hazards reduce performance: structural hazards (resource conflicts), data hazards (an instruction needs a result not yet produced) and control hazards (branches). Solutions are stalling, forwarding (bypassing), branch prediction and register renaming. Instruction level parallelism is exploited by scalar and superscalar pipelines that issue several instructions per cycle, using compilation techniques such as loop unrolling and instruction scheduling. Thread level parallelism uses many threads on multicore processors, while data level parallelism applies one operation to many data items using vector or SIMD units.
sla_notes_illustrations: Without pipelining, 100 instructions of 5 cycles each need 500 cycles. With a 5-stage pipeline they need 5 + 99 = 104 cycles, a speedup of about 4.8.
sla_notes_daily_life: A factory assembly line is a similar idea: while one car is being painted the next is being assembled, so more cars are finished per hour.
sla_exercise: Name the five stages of a classic pipeline.::Instruction fetch, decode, execute, memory access and write back.||What is a data hazard and how can forwarding help?::A data hazard happens when an instruction needs a result not yet produced; forwarding passes the result directly from a pipeline stage to the next instruction.||Calculate the number of cycles needed for 10 instructions in a 4-stage pipeline.::4 + 10 - 1 = 13 cycles.

sla_assessment_criteria: Understanding of Reference models and transmission media, wireless transmission, the public switched telephone networks, mobile telephone system and Network protocols is properly demonstrated.
sla_teaching_aids: Network devices (Router|Switch|Bridge|Repeater|Hub|Gateway|Etc.)|Packet tracer|Internet resources|Flip charts|Braille devices|Simulators (Celiot|Celiot++|Jeliot|Etc)|Computer system|Modals|Video tutorials|Marker pens|Non- Visual Desktop Access (NVDA)|Virtual Reality (VR)/Augmented Reality (AR) tools|Security Operations Center (SOC) Simulator|Simulator creation tools
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Networking models divide communication into layers so that different systems and products can interoperate. This activity covers the OSI and TCP/IP reference models, transmission media and common protocols.
sla_notes_details: The OSI model has seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation and application. The TCP/IP model has four layers: network access (link), internet, transport and application. Guided transmission media are twisted pair, coaxial and fibre optic cables; wireless transmission uses radio waves, microwaves, infrared and satellite links. The public switched telephone network (PSTN) uses circuit switching, while the mobile telephone system is cellular, evolving through 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G. Protocols include HTTP (web pages), FTP (file transfer), IP (addressing and routing) and PPP (point-to-point links over serial lines and dial-up).
sla_notes_illustrations: When a learner opens a web page, HTTP at the application layer creates a request, TCP splits it into segments, IP adds addresses, and the network access layer sends bits over Wi-Fi or fibre.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding the layers helps a technician find faults: no cable link is a physical layer problem, while a wrong IP address is a network layer problem.
sla_exercise: List the four layers of the TCP/IP model.::Network access, internet, transport and application.||Which layer of the OSI model deals with routing?::The network layer.||Name two guided transmission media.::Twisted pair cable and fibre optic cable.

learning_activity_name: Develop understanding of Data link layer (Switched LANs: Link-Layer Addressing and ARP, Ethernet, Link-Layer, Switches, VLANs)
sla_name: Data link layer
sla_assessment_criteria: Understanding of Data link layer is correctly developed.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The data link layer transfers frames between directly connected nodes and detects errors on the link. It is the layer at which Ethernet and switches operate.
sla_notes_details: Link-layer addressing uses 48-bit MAC addresses burnt into network cards. ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) finds the MAC address that corresponds to a known IP address on the same LAN. Ethernet is the dominant wired LAN technology using frames with destination, source, type, data and a CRC error check; it originally used CSMA/CD to share the medium. A switch learns MAC addresses, keeps a forwarding table and sends frames only to the correct port, unlike a hub that repeats to all ports. VLANs (virtual LANs) divide one physical switch into several logical networks to improve security and reduce broadcasts.
sla_notes_illustrations: If host A knows the IP address of host B but not its MAC address, it broadcasts an ARP request; B replies with its MAC address and A stores it in its ARP cache.
sla_notes_daily_life: In a school, a VLAN can separate the administration computers from the student laboratory even though they use the same switches.
sla_exercise: What is the function of ARP?::To map an IP address to the corresponding MAC address on a local network.||How does a switch differ from a hub?::A switch forwards frames only to the destination port using a MAC table, while a hub broadcasts to all ports.||State the purpose of a VLAN.::To divide a physical network into separate logical networks for security and to limit broadcast traffic.

learning_activity_name: Create a network that make use of wireless or Ethernet technology
sla_name: Creating a network using wireless or Ethernet technology
sla_method: Practical or Collaborative Project work/ Simulation
sla_assessment_criteria: The network that make use of wireless or Ethernet technology is correctly created.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners apply networking knowledge practically by designing and setting up a small local area network using Ethernet cables or Wi-Fi.
sla_notes_details: The steps are: plan the topology (star is most common) and list devices; connect computers to a switch with straight-through UTP cables terminated with RJ45 connectors, or connect them wirelessly to an access point; assign IP addresses manually or through a DHCP server within the same subnet (for example 192.168.1.0/24 with mask 255.255.255.0); configure the default gateway and DNS; test connectivity with the ping command; and share resources such as files and a printer. For wireless networks configure the SSID, security (WPA2 or WPA3) and channel. Document the network with a diagram and record test results.
sla_notes_illustrations: Four computers are connected to an 8-port switch and given the addresses 192.168.1.10 to 192.168.1.13. The command ping 192.168.1.12 from the first computer returns replies, proving the link works.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill is used to set up a small office, school laboratory or cyber cafe network and to share an internet connection.
sla_exercise: Which connector is used at the end of a UTP Ethernet cable?::The RJ45 connector.||Which command tests whether another computer is reachable?::The ping command.||State one security setting for a Wi-Fi network.::Use WPA2 or WPA3 encryption with a strong password.

learning_activity_name: Develop understanding of Network layer (design issues, routing algorithms, Congestion control algorithms, Internetworking, the network layer in the internet (IPv4 and IPv6), Quality of Service)
sla_name: Network layer
sla_assessment_criteria: Understanding of Network layer is correctly developed.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The network layer moves packets from a source host to a destination host across many networks. It provides logical addressing and routing.
sla_notes_details: Design issues include store-and-forward packet switching, connection-oriented versus connectionless service and the services offered to the transport layer. Routing algorithms decide the path: static routing, shortest path (Dijkstra), distance vector (Bellman-Ford, used in RIP) and link state (used in OSPF). Congestion control algorithms prevent too many packets from overloading the network, using traffic shaping, choke packets and load shedding. Internetworking connects different networks using routers and tunnelling. In the Internet, IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (about 4.3 billion) and IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses to solve address exhaustion; subnetting and NAT extend IPv4. Quality of Service (QoS) gives priority to time-sensitive traffic such as voice and video.
sla_notes_illustrations: A packet from Dar es Salaam to Mwanza passes through several routers; each router reads the destination IP address, consults its routing table and forwards the packet to the next hop.
sla_notes_daily_life: Internet service providers use routing and QoS so that video calls remain smooth even when many people download files.
sla_exercise: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?::128 bits.||Name one distance vector routing protocol.::RIP (Routing Information Protocol).||What is the purpose of congestion control?::To prevent too many packets from overloading the network and causing loss and delay.

learning_activity_name: Elaborate the transport layer (Transport service, elements of transport protocol, Simple Transport Protocol, Internet transport layer protocols: UDP and TCP)
sla_name: Transport layer
sla_assessment_criteria: The transport layer is properly elaborated.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The transport layer provides end-to-end communication between processes on different hosts. It uses port numbers to deliver data to the correct application.
sla_notes_details: Transport services include segmentation, multiplexing, flow control, error control and connection management. TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is connection-oriented and reliable: it uses a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmission, sliding window flow control and congestion control. UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless and unreliable but fast and has low overhead, used for streaming, DNS queries and online games. Elements of a transport protocol include addressing, connection establishment and release, and buffering. A simple transport protocol sends data segments and waits for acknowledgements before continuing. Well known ports include 80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS and 25 for SMTP.
sla_notes_illustrations: A video call uses UDP because a lost frame is not worth resending, while downloading a file uses TCP because every byte must arrive correctly and in order.
sla_notes_daily_life: When a bank website loads securely, TCP guarantees that the whole page and transaction data arrive completely and in order.
sla_exercise: Name the three steps of the TCP handshake.::SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK.||State one difference between TCP and UDP.::TCP is reliable and connection-oriented, while UDP is unreliable and connectionless.||Which port number does HTTPS normally use?::Port 443.

learning_activity_name: Describe the application layer (Domain name system, electronic mail, World Wide Web: architecture; dynamic web document and http)
sla_name: Application layer
sla_assessment_criteria: Application layer is clearly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The application layer provides network services directly to user programs such as browsers and email clients. It contains the protocols users interact with most.
sla_notes_details: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates domain names such as tie.go.tz into IP addresses using a hierarchy of root, top-level domain and authoritative servers. Electronic mail uses SMTP to send, and POP3 or IMAP to retrieve messages, with user agents and message transfer agents. The World Wide Web architecture is a client-server system in which browsers request pages from web servers using URLs and HTTP; the response contains HTML, CSS and scripts. Static documents are stored files, while dynamic web documents are generated by server-side programs (PHP, Python) or by client-side scripts (JavaScript). HTTP methods include GET and POST, and status codes such as 200 (OK) and 404 (not found).
sla_notes_illustrations: Typing www.example.com causes the browser to ask the DNS for the IP address, open a TCP connection, send GET / HTTP/1.1 and display the HTML returned with status code 200.
sla_notes_daily_life: Every time people send email, open a website or use online banking, application layer protocols are working.
sla_exercise: What is the role of DNS?::To translate domain names into IP addresses.||Which protocols are used to retrieve email?::POP3 and IMAP.||What does HTTP status code 404 mean?::The requested page or resource was not found.

sla_name: Network security principles, tools and protocols
sla_assessment_criteria: Network security principles, tools and protocols in computer network are applied correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Network security protects data and network resources from unauthorised access, misuse and attack. It is built on confidentiality, integrity and availability.
sla_notes_details: Common threats are malware, phishing, denial of service, man-in-the-middle attacks, eavesdropping and password cracking. Security tools include firewalls that filter traffic by rules, intrusion detection and prevention systems, antivirus software, virtual private networks (VPNs) and access control lists. Cryptography provides confidentiality through symmetric encryption (AES) and asymmetric encryption (RSA); hashing (SHA-256) gives integrity; digital signatures and certificates provide authentication and non-repudiation. Security protocols include SSL/TLS for HTTPS, IPsec for VPNs, SSH for remote login and WPA2 for Wi-Fi. Good practice includes strong passwords, multi-factor authentication, regular updates and backups.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a school laboratory a firewall is configured to block social media sites, a VPN is used for a remote teacher to reach the school server, and the server uses HTTPS so that passwords are encrypted.
sla_notes_daily_life: Mobile banking and online shopping depend on TLS encryption and authentication to protect money and personal information.
sla_exercise: Name the three goals of security (CIA triad).::Confidentiality, integrity and availability.||What is the function of a firewall?::To filter incoming and outgoing network traffic according to security rules.||Which protocol secures websites in HTTPS?::SSL/TLS (Transport Layer Security).

sla_notes_intro: Object Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that organises software around objects, which combine data (attributes) and behaviour (methods). It is supported by languages such as C++, Java and Python.
sla_notes_details: OOP differs from procedure oriented programming, which organises a program as functions acting on separate data. The four main concepts are encapsulation (bundling data and methods and hiding details using access control), inheritance (a class acquiring attributes and methods of a parent class), polymorphism (one interface, many forms, through overloading and overriding) and abstraction. Composition builds a class from objects of other classes (a has-a relationship). Benefits include reuse, easier maintenance, modularity and modelling real-world things. The basic elements of a program include: structure (in Java a class with a main method; in C++ include directives and namespaces; Python uses indentation), output and input statements, data types (int, float, char, bool, string), type conversion, tokens, identifiers (names chosen by the programmer), variables, constants, operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment) and control structures (if, switch) and loops (for, while, do-while).
sla_notes_illustrations: A class Student has attributes name and marks and a method average(). Objects s1 and s2 are created from it. A class Graduate can inherit Student and add the attribute degree, reusing the existing code.
sla_notes_daily_life: Apps such as mobile games and school management systems are built with objects like Player, Teacher and Student, which makes them easier to extend.
sla_exercise: Name the four main concepts of OOP.::Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction.||Differentiate a class from an object.::A class is a blueprint or template, while an object is an instance created from the class.||Write a loop in Python that prints numbers 1 to 3.::for i in range(1, 4): print(i)

sla_notes_intro: Every object oriented program follows a definite structure that organises classes, their members and the entry point of execution. Learners identify these parts in C++, Java and Python.
sla_notes_details: A program normally has: import or include statements for libraries; class definitions containing data members (fields), constructors (special methods that initialise objects), methods (member functions) and access specifiers (public, private, protected); and a main entry point that creates objects and calls their methods. In Java the entry is public static void main(String[] args) inside a class; in C++ it is int main() with the include directive and using namespace std; in Python the code usually ends with an if __name__ equal to __main__ block. Comments document the code. Classes are often kept in separate files or modules, and objects communicate by calling each other's methods.
sla_notes_illustrations: In Java: class Account with a private double balance, a constructor Account(double b), and methods deposit() and getBalance(). The main method creates Account a = new Account(500) and calls a.deposit(200).
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding structure helps a programmer read other people's code and organise large projects such as a school records system.
sla_exercise: What is the purpose of a constructor?::To initialise the data members of an object when it is created.||Name the entry point method of a Java program.::The main method.||What is the use of the private access specifier?::It restricts access to a member so it can be used only inside its own class.

sla_notes_intro: Learners apply the syntax and constructs of an object oriented language to write working programs. This is a practical activity done with a compiler or interpreter.
sla_notes_details: Steps: define the problem, identify classes and their attributes and methods, write the class definitions with constructors, create objects, and use inheritance and polymorphism where appropriate. Syntax examples: in Python, class Circle: with def __init__(self, r): self.r = r and def area(self): return 3.14 * self.r * self.r; in Java, class Circle { double r; double area() { return 3.14 * r * r; } }; inheritance in Java uses the extends keyword and in C++ a colon with the base class name. Overriding means a subclass defines a method with the same signature as its parent, and overloading means several methods have the same name but different parameters. Programs are compiled or interpreted, run and tested with sample data.
sla_notes_illustrations: A Shape base class has a method area(). Subclasses Rectangle and Circle override area(). A list of Shape objects is looped through and each object calls area(), and the correct version runs for each: polymorphism in action.
sla_notes_daily_life: Software for a bank, a shop point of sale or a hospital uses these constructs to represent customers, products and patients.

sla_assessment_criteria: Object Oriented programs using appropriate skills are correctly debugged.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Debugging is the process of finding and correcting errors in a program. Object oriented programs need systematic debugging skills because errors can be hidden in class interactions.
sla_notes_details: There are three types of errors: syntax errors (violating language rules, reported by the compiler), runtime errors (such as dividing by zero, null reference, index out of range) and logic errors (the program runs but gives wrong results). Techniques include reading error messages, tracing with print statements, using an IDE debugger with breakpoints, stepping through code and watching variable values, rubber duck reasoning, unit testing individual methods and using exception handling with try, catch or except blocks. Good practice is to test with normal, boundary and invalid data and to keep methods short so that faults are easy to locate.
sla_notes_illustrations: A Java program throws NullPointerException because an object was declared but not created with new. Placing a breakpoint on that line shows the variable is null; adding the statement s = new Student() fixes it.
sla_notes_daily_life: Professional developers debug daily to make sure apps do not crash, for example in mobile money apps where a logic error could give a wrong balance.
sla_exercise: Name the three types of programming errors.::Syntax errors, runtime errors and logic errors.||What is a breakpoint?::A marked line where the debugger pauses execution so the programmer can inspect variables.||Why should a program be tested with boundary data?::Errors often occur at the limits of allowed values, so boundary tests find them.

sla_assessment_criteria: The concepts, structure and design of operating systems is properly described.
sla_teaching_aids: Internet resources|NVDA|Braille devices|Flip charts|Marker pen|Video tutorials|Projector|Computer system|Benchmarking tools
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages hardware resources and provides services for application programs. It acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware.
sla_notes_details: The evolution of operating systems moved from no OS and batch systems, to multiprogramming and time-sharing, then to personal computer, network, distributed, real-time and mobile operating systems. Types include batch, time-sharing, multitasking, multiprocessing, distributed, real-time and embedded. The architecture and structure can be monolithic (all services in the kernel, as in traditional Unix), layered, microkernel (minimal kernel, other services in user space) or modular, and hybrid systems combine these. Design goals include efficiency, reliability, security, portability and convenience. The main functions are process management, memory management, file management, device management, security and user interface.
sla_notes_illustrations: Linux uses a modular monolithic kernel, while Minix and QNX use a microkernel. A microkernel is more reliable because a failing driver does not crash the whole system.
sla_notes_daily_life: Android, Windows and Linux are operating systems used on phones, computers and servers, and real-time operating systems control car braking systems and hospital monitors.
sla_exercise: Define an operating system.::System software that manages hardware and software resources and provides services to programs and users.||Name two OS structures.::Monolithic and microkernel (or layered).||Give one example of a real-time operating system use.::Controlling an aircraft or a car braking system.

sla_assessment_criteria: The impact of operating system design on application system design and performance is correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The design of an operating system determines how efficiently applications run and what facilities they can use. This activity relates OS design choices to application behaviour.
sla_notes_details: System calls form the interface through which applications request OS services, and their cost depends on kernel design. Scheduling policy affects responsiveness and throughput, memory management affects how many programs can run at once and how fast, and file system design affects loading and saving speeds. A monolithic kernel is fast because of fewer context switches, but a bug can crash the system; a microkernel is safer but has more message passing overhead. Portability is improved through abstraction layers and standard APIs such as POSIX. Application developers must consider concurrency support (threads), memory limits, security permissions and driver availability. Performance is measured by throughput, response time, turnaround time and resource utilisation.
sla_notes_illustrations: A program that opens 1000 small files individually spends more time in system calls than a program that reads one large file; the developer can improve performance by buffering.
sla_notes_daily_life: A phone running a lightweight OS can run well on 2 GB of RAM, while a heavy OS on the same hardware would be slow, which explains why apps run differently across devices.
sla_exercise: What is a system call?::A request from an application program to the operating system for a service.||State one advantage of a microkernel.::It is more reliable and secure because most services run outside the kernel.||Name two measures of OS performance.::Throughput and response time (or turnaround time).

sla_assessment_criteria: Competency in recognizing and using operating system design and performance is correctly demonstrated.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners develop competence in the main functions of an operating system: managing processes, the CPU, memory, files and input-output devices.
sla_notes_details: A process is a program in execution; it moves between the new, ready, running, waiting and terminated states, and has a process control block. Threads are lightweight units of execution within a process. Processes cooperate through synchronisation (semaphores, mutex) and communication (pipes, shared memory, message passing). CPU scheduling algorithms are FCFS, shortest job first, priority and round robin. Deadlock occurs when processes wait for each other forever; it is handled by prevention, avoidance (banker's algorithm) and detection and recovery. Memory management uses paging and segmentation and virtual memory with demand paging and page replacement (FIFO, LRU). File systems organise data in directories and use allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed). Device management uses drivers, buffering, caching and spooling.
sla_notes_illustrations: Round robin with time quantum 2 for processes P1 (burst 4) and P2 (burst 3): P1 runs 2, P2 runs 2, P1 runs 2 (finishes at 6), P2 runs 1 (finishes at 7). Average waiting time is (2 + 4) divided by 2 = 3.
sla_notes_daily_life: When many apps are open on a phone, scheduling and memory management decide which app gets the CPU and which is moved out of memory.
sla_exercise: Name the states of a process.::New, ready, running, waiting and terminated.||What is deadlock?::A situation in which processes wait for each other indefinitely for resources.||Which scheduling algorithm gives each process a fixed time slice?::Round robin.

sla_notes_intro: This activity introduces the main concepts of modern database systems: relational design, the ER model, SQL, NoSQL, big data and data warehouses.
sla_notes_details: The relational model stores data in tables (relations) of rows and columns, with primary keys identifying rows and foreign keys linking tables. The Entity-Relationship (ER) model represents entities, attributes and relationships (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many). SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to define data (CREATE, ALTER), manipulate data (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), query (SELECT) and control access (GRANT). NoSQL databases (document, key-value, column and graph stores such as MongoDB and Redis) handle flexible, large-scale and unstructured data. Big data is characterised by volume, velocity and variety. A data warehouse is a central repository of integrated historical data from many sources used for analysis and reporting.
sla_notes_illustrations: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 70 ORDER BY marks DESC; returns the names and marks of students who scored above 70, highest first.
sla_notes_daily_life: Banks use relational databases for accounts, social media uses NoSQL and big data for posts and images, and retail chains use data warehouses to analyse sales.
sla_exercise: What is a primary key?::A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table.||Write an SQL statement to select all rows from a table called pupils.::SELECT * FROM pupils;||State the three Vs of big data.::Volume, velocity and variety.

sla_notes_intro: Database design is the process of organising data so that it is stored efficiently, consistently and can be retrieved easily. It follows three levels: conceptual, logical and physical.
sla_notes_details: Conceptual design produces an ER diagram independent of software. Logical design converts the ER diagram into relations with keys and constraints. Physical design decides file structures, data types, indexes and storage in a chosen DBMS. Normalisation reduces redundancy and anomalies: first normal form (atomic values, no repeating groups), second normal form (no partial dependency on part of a composite key) and third normal form (no transitive dependency). The steps are gather requirements, identify entities and attributes, define relationships and cardinality, draw the ER diagram, map to tables, normalise, and implement using SQL.
sla_notes_illustrations: A table with columns StudentID, Name, CourseCode, CourseName repeats course names. Splitting it into Student, Course and Enrolment tables removes redundancy and update anomalies, reaching third normal form.
sla_notes_daily_life: A well designed database lets a school store students, teachers and results without duplication, so a change of phone number is made only once.
sla_exercise: Name the three levels of database design.::Conceptual, logical and physical.||What is the aim of normalisation?::To reduce data redundancy and avoid update, insert and delete anomalies.||State the rule of first normal form.::Each field must contain only atomic (single) values with no repeating groups.

sla_notes_intro: A database model defines the logical structure of a database and how data is stored, related and manipulated. Different models suit different kinds of applications.
sla_notes_details: The hierarchical model arranges data in a tree of parent and child records. The network model allows many-to-many links using sets and pointers. The relational model uses tables and is the most widely used. The object-oriented model stores objects with attributes and methods, and the object-relational model extends relational systems with object features. Modern models include document, key-value, column-family and graph models. Comparison is based on structure, flexibility, query language, integrity support and performance. The relational model offers ACID transactions (atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability), while many NoSQL models follow the BASE approach for scalability.
sla_notes_illustrations: An organisation chart naturally fits the hierarchical model, a social network of friends fits the graph model, and a payroll system fits the relational model.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choosing the right model saves cost: a shop uses relational tables for sales, while a music streaming service uses graph or document models to recommend songs.
sla_exercise: Name the database model that uses tables.::The relational model.||What does ACID stand for?::Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.||Give one example of a suitable use of a graph database.::Modelling social networks or friend relationships.

sla_notes_intro: A database management system (DBMS) is software that creates, stores and controls access to databases. Parallel and distributed DBMSs improve speed, capacity and availability.
sla_notes_details: A parallel DBMS uses multiple processors, disks and memory in one system to run queries simultaneously; architectures are shared memory, shared disk and shared nothing. A distributed DBMS stores data on several computers in different locations linked by a network and appears as one database to users. Techniques include fragmentation (horizontal and vertical), replication (copies on several sites) and distributed transactions using two-phase commit. Advantages are speed, reliability, scalability and local control; disadvantages are complexity, cost, security and the difficulty of keeping copies consistent. Examples are Oracle RAC, Google Spanner and Cassandra.
sla_notes_illustrations: A bank stores customer records in branch databases in Arusha, Mbeya and Dar es Salaam. A query for the total balance combines data from the three sites, but a customer sees one system.
sla_notes_daily_life: Mobile money companies replicate data on several servers so that services continue if one server fails.
sla_exercise: What is replication in a distributed database?::Keeping copies of the same data at several sites.||Name one architecture of parallel DBMS.::Shared nothing (or shared memory or shared disk).||State one disadvantage of distributed databases.::They are complex and it is difficult to keep data consistent across sites.

sla_notes_intro: Databases are evolving to meet the demands of big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence. This activity explores the newest trends and how they are applied.
sla_notes_details: Emerging models include NoSQL types (document databases like MongoDB, key-value stores like Redis, wide column stores like Cassandra, graph databases like Neo4j), NewSQL systems that combine SQL with scalability, in-memory databases for very fast analytics, time-series databases for sensor data and blockchain ledgers. Technologies include cloud databases as a service, data lakes, data mining, real-time analytics and machine learning integration. Applications are e-commerce recommendations, fraud detection in banking, Internet of Things monitoring, health records, smart agriculture and social media. Issues include data privacy law, security and ethics.
sla_notes_illustrations: A time-series database stores temperature readings from sensors in a greenhouse every minute, so a farmer can see trends and receive alerts when temperature exceeds a limit.
sla_notes_daily_life: Streaming services suggest films using graph and document databases, and banks use real-time databases to detect suspicious card transactions within seconds.
sla_exercise: Name one type of NoSQL database and an example.::Document database such as MongoDB.||What data is best stored in a time-series database?::Data recorded at regular time intervals such as sensor readings.||State one application of emerging database technology.::Fraud detection in banking (or recommendations in e-commerce).

Forms collect data through the POST method and PHP inserts it in the table. Test each operation: create, read, update and delete (CRUD).

sla_notes_intro: A web application is a program that runs on a web server and is accessed through a browser over the Internet or an intranet. Unlike a static website, it processes user input and produces dynamic results.
sla_notes_details: Web applications developed from simple static pages of the early web (1990s), through server-side scripting (CGI, PHP, ASP), to AJAX and single page applications and modern frameworks. Types include static, dynamic, e-commerce, portal, content management and progressive web applications. A website mainly presents information, while a web application allows interaction and data processing (login, payments, dashboards). Front-end technologies are HTML tags for structure, CSS for style and JavaScript for behaviour; back-end technologies are PHP, Python, Node.js and databases. An Application Programming Interface (API) allows programs to communicate with each other, for example REST APIs returning JSON. Frameworks and libraries such as React, Angular and Django speed up development.
sla_notes_illustrations: An online school portal is a web application: a learner logs in, the server checks the user in the database, and a page with that learner's results is generated.
sla_notes_daily_life: Everyday examples are online banking, e-government services such as tax portals, ride hailing and online exam registration.
sla_exercise: State one difference between a website and a web application.::A website mainly displays information, while a web application allows users to interact with it and processes their data.||What does API stand for?::Application Programming Interface.||Name two front-end technologies.::HTML and CSS (or JavaScript).

sla_notes_intro: Interactive web pages respond to user actions such as clicks and typing. Responsive techniques make pages display well on phones, tablets and computers.
sla_notes_details: HTML defines the elements, CSS controls appearance and JavaScript manipulates the page through the Document Object Model (DOM): it can change text, hide or show elements, handle events (click, submit, keyup), validate forms and update content without reloading. Responsive design uses the viewport meta tag, flexible percentage widths, CSS media queries, flexbox and grid layouts, and scalable images. The steps are: plan the layout, write semantic HTML, style with CSS, add JavaScript for events, test on different screen sizes and validate. In PHP or Python, forms are processed on the server to generate the response.
sla_notes_illustrations: A button with id show is clicked; a JavaScript function uses document.getElementById to toggle the display of a paragraph. A media query at max-width 600px changes a three-column layout into one column.
sla_notes_daily_life: Websites that adjust on a phone, such as news sites and online shops, use these techniques because most people in Tanzania browse with mobile phones.

sla_notes_intro: Web APIs are interfaces built into browsers or provided by servers that give web applications powerful features such as drawing, drag and drop and communication with servers.
sla_notes_details: The Canvas API allows drawing graphics: add a canvas element in HTML, obtain its context with getContext('2d'), and draw shapes, text and images using methods such as fillRect, arc, lineTo and drawImage, and animate with requestAnimationFrame. The Drag and Drop API uses attribute draggable and events dragstart, dragover and drop with dataTransfer to move elements. Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style in which resources are identified by URLs and manipulated using HTTP methods that match CRUD operations: POST creates, GET reads, PUT or PATCH updates and DELETE removes. Data is commonly exchanged as JSON using fetch.
sla_notes_illustrations: A canvas of 300 by 150 pixels: ctx.fillStyle = 'green' and ctx.fillRect(10, 10, 100, 50) draws a green rectangle. A fetch call to /api/students with GET returns a JSON list of students.

Development uses tools such as Node.js, npm, bundlers and version control. The steps are: choose a framework, create the project, design components, manage state, connect to an API, test and deploy.

sla_notes_intro: The back end is the server-side part of a web application that handles requests, applies business rules, stores information and controls security.
sla_notes_details: Back-end languages include PHP, Python, JavaScript (Node.js). The server receives HTTP requests, processes user input from forms (GET and POST), validates and sanitises it, interacts with databases, and returns a response using template output such as HTML or JSON. Secure user accounts require registration and login, hashing passwords (for example password_hash in PHP or bcrypt), sessions or tokens to keep users logged in, role based access control, HTTPS and protection against SQL injection, cross-site scripting and cross-site request forgery. Good structure separates models, views and controllers (MVC).

sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A data structure is a way of organising and storing data so that it can be used efficiently. An algorithm is a finite sequence of well defined steps to solve a problem.
sla_notes_details: Data structures are classified as primitive (integer, character) and non-primitive; non-primitive ones are linear (arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues) and non-linear (trees, graphs, hash tables). Characteristics of an algorithm are input, output, definiteness, finiteness and effectiveness. Algorithms are expressed as pseudocode or flowcharts. An abstract data type (ADT) defines operations without implementation. The choice of data structure affects the speed and memory used, so programs combine suitable structures with efficient algorithms. Program = data structures + algorithms.
sla_notes_illustrations: To find a contact in a phone, a sorted list with binary search is fast; storing contacts in a hash table gives even faster lookup by name.
sla_notes_daily_life: Maps, search engines and social networks depend on good data structures and algorithms to give results in milliseconds.
sla_exercise: Define an algorithm.::A finite sequence of well defined steps for solving a problem.||Name two linear data structures.::Stack and queue (or array or linked list).||Is a tree a linear or non-linear data structure?::Non-linear.

sla_name: Basic data structures: linked lists, stacks, queues and trees
sla_assessment_criteria: Basic data structure is explored and utilized correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: This activity explores the structure and operations of linked lists, stacks, queues and trees.
sla_notes_details: A linked list is a sequence of nodes, each holding data and a pointer to the next node; it allows easy insertion and deletion without shifting elements, but access is sequential. Variants are singly, doubly and circular linked lists. A stack is a last in first out (LIFO) structure with push, pop and peek; it is used for undo and function calls. A queue is first in first out (FIFO) with enqueue and dequeue; it is used in printing and scheduling. A tree is a hierarchy of nodes with a root and children; a binary tree has at most two children per node, and a binary search tree keeps smaller values on the left and larger on the right. Tree traversals are preorder, inorder and postorder.
sla_notes_illustrations: Push 5, push 8, push 2 onto a stack then pop gives 2, the last item added. Inserting 50, 30, 70, 20 in a binary search tree places 30 left of 50, 70 right of 50 and 20 left of 30; an inorder traversal gives 20, 30, 50, 70.
sla_notes_daily_life: The back button in a browser uses a stack, a queue of customers at a bank counter uses FIFO, and a computer folder system is a tree.
sla_exercise: State the order in which a stack removes items.::Last in first out (LIFO).||What does a node of a singly linked list contain?::Data and a pointer to the next node.||Give the inorder traversal of a binary search tree with 4 at the root, 2 on the left and 6 on the right.::2, 4, 6.

sla_name: Searching and sorting algorithms
sla_assessment_criteria: Design and performance of various classic searching and sorting algorithms is correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Searching finds an item in a collection and sorting arranges items in order. Classic algorithms differ in design and performance.
sla_notes_details: Linear search checks each element in turn (O(n)); binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list (O(log n)). Sorting algorithms include bubble sort, selection sort and insertion sort (simple, O(n squared)), and merge sort and quick sort (efficient, O(n log n) on average). Merge sort uses divide and conquer and needs extra memory; quick sort partitions around a pivot. Stability, memory use and best, average and worst case performance are compared. Performance is judged by the number of comparisons and swaps and the running time on different input sizes.
sla_notes_illustrations: Binary search for 23 in 4, 9, 15, 23, 31, 40, 52: middle is 23 found in one step. For 40: middle 23 is smaller, look right half 31, 40, 52, middle 40 found in two steps.
sla_notes_daily_life: Online shops sort products by price and search engines search large sorted indexes so results appear quickly.
sla_exercise: What is the worst case time of bubble sort?::O(n squared).||What condition is needed for binary search?::The list must be sorted.||Name a divide and conquer sorting algorithm.::Merge sort (or quick sort).

sla_name: Programming sorting algorithms and performance reports
sla_assessment_criteria: A program that implements various sorting algorithms and create a report for performance is correctly written.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners implement sorting algorithms in a programming language, measure their performance and write a report of the results.
sla_notes_details: Implement bubble sort, insertion sort, merge sort and quick sort in Python, Java or C++ as functions that take an array. Generate test data of different sizes (100, 1000, 10000) and types (random, sorted, reverse sorted). Measure running time using timing functions (time.perf_counter in Python) and count comparisons and swaps. Record the results in a table and draw graphs of time against size. The report includes the objective, method, code description, results, analysis (which algorithm is fastest and why, matching with theoretical complexity), and conclusion with recommendations.
sla_notes_illustrations: For 10000 random numbers a bubble sort takes several seconds while merge sort takes a few milliseconds, which agrees with the O(n squared) versus O(n log n) analysis.
sla_notes_daily_life: Software developers benchmark algorithms in this way before choosing one for a system with a large amount of data such as a national exam database.
sla_exercise: Why should test data of different sizes be used?::To see how running time grows with the input size.||Name two things to count when measuring a sorting algorithm.::Comparisons and swaps.||What should a performance report conclude?::Which algorithm performs best and why, supported by the results.

sla_assessment_criteria: A program that implements a linked list data structure is correctly created.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Arrays and linked lists are basic containers. Learners create both using classes and compare them.
sla_notes_details: An array stores elements of the same type in contiguous memory with constant time access by index but fixed size in many languages; dynamic arrays such as ArrayList or Python lists resize automatically. A linked list is implemented with a Node class holding data and a next reference, and a LinkedList class holding the head with methods insert at head, insert at end, delete, search and display. Operations on an array cost O(n) for insertion in the middle, while a linked list inserts in O(1) once the position is known, but search is O(n). Steps: define the Node class, define the list class, implement methods, test with different data and compare the two structures.
sla_notes_illustrations: In Python: class Node with data and next; class LinkedList with head. Calling insert_head(5), insert_head(8) gives the list 8 to 5; display() prints 8, 5.
sla_notes_daily_life: A music playlist that allows songs to be added and removed easily can be implemented with a linked list.
sla_exercise: What is the advantage of an array?::Fast access to any element by its index.||What does the last node of a singly linked list point to?::Null (none).||Which is faster for inserting at the front, an array or a linked list?::A linked list.

learning_activity_name: Implement stack and queue, binary search tree , balanced tree (such as an AVL tree), graph, hash table data structures in object-oriented programming language.
sla_name: Implementing stacks, queues, trees, graphs and hash tables
sla_method: Practical/ Simulation/ virtual lab/ video tutorials
sla_assessment_criteria: Stack and queue, binary search tree, balanced tree (such as an AVL tree), graph, hash table data structures is correctly implemented.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners implement advanced data structures using an object oriented language: stacks, queues, binary search trees, AVL trees, graphs and hash tables.
sla_notes_details: A stack and a queue can be implemented with arrays or linked lists with methods push, pop, enqueue and dequeue and checks for empty and full. A binary search tree class has insert, search and traversal methods. An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree where the balance factor (height of left minus right) of every node is -1, 0 or 1; rotations (left, right, left-right, right-left) restore balance after insertion or deletion, guaranteeing O(log n) operations. A graph is stored as an adjacency list or adjacency matrix with traversals breadth first search (using a queue) and depth first search (using a stack). A hash table maps keys to array indices with a hash function, and collisions are resolved by chaining or open addressing.
sla_notes_illustrations: Hash function h(key) = key mod 10 places 25 at index 5 and 35 also at index 5 (a collision); with chaining, both are stored in a list at index 5.
sla_notes_daily_life: Undo features use stacks, route finding uses graphs, and dictionaries or contact lists use hash tables for fast lookup.
sla_exercise: What is a collision in a hash table?::When two different keys are mapped to the same index.||Which data structure is used in breadth first search?::A queue.||What is the allowed balance factor of an AVL tree node?::-1, 0 or 1.

learning_activity_name: Describe the techniques of algorithm analysis
sla_name: Techniques of algorithm analysis
sla_assessment_criteria: The techniques of algorithm analysis is correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Algorithm analysis measures the resources (time and memory) an algorithm needs as the input size grows. It allows comparison of algorithms independent of hardware.
sla_notes_details: Time complexity is expressed with asymptotic notation: Big O gives an upper bound, Omega a lower bound and Theta a tight bound. Common growth rates from best to worst are O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic, O(n) linear, O(n log n), O(n squared) quadratic, O(2 to the n) exponential. To analyse an algorithm count the basic operations, ignore constants and lower order terms; a single loop is O(n), two nested loops O(n squared), and halving each step O(log n). Best, average and worst cases are considered. Space complexity measures extra memory. Recurrence relations are used for recursive algorithms, for example merge sort T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n giving O(n log n).
sla_notes_illustrations: For a program with a loop from 1 to n containing another loop from 1 to n, the statement inside runs n times n = n squared times, so the complexity is O(n squared).
sla_notes_daily_life: Developers use analysis to decide whether a program will handle one million users before it is built.
sla_exercise: What does Big O notation describe?::The upper bound on the growth of an algorithm's running time or space as input grows.||What is the complexity of binary search?::O(log n).||Give the complexity of two nested loops each running n times.::O(n squared).

sla_teaching_aids: Automated systems|Virtual lab|Simulations|Microprocessors|Computer systems|Internet resources|NVDA|Braille devices|AI Platforms or tools (ChartGPT|Etc)|Prolog software|Computer|Simulator (Celiot|Celiot++|Jeliot
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: An automated system performs tasks with little or no human intervention. It uses sensors, a processing unit and actuators working together.
sla_notes_details: A sensor detects a physical quantity (temperature, light, moisture, distance, pressure) and converts it into an electrical signal. A microprocessor or microcontroller (for example Arduino or Raspberry Pi) reads the signal, compares it with set values and decides what to do using a program. An actuator (motor, relay, valve, buzzer, heater) carries out the action. The system may use open loop control (no feedback) or closed loop control with feedback. Analogue signals are converted with ADC and digital signals sent out through DAC or output pins. The outline of a system includes inputs, process, outputs, features and functionality.
sla_notes_illustrations: An automatic street light: a light sensor (LDR) sends a value; when it is below a threshold the microcontroller switches on the lamp through a relay.
sla_notes_daily_life: Automatic doors, water pumps controlled by tank level sensors, and traffic lights are common examples.
sla_exercise: Name the three main parts of an automated system.::Sensor, processor (microprocessor or microcontroller) and actuator.||What is the role of an actuator?::To perform a physical action such as moving or switching on a device.||What is closed loop control?::A control system that uses feedback from the output to adjust its operation.

sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Automation has benefits and drawbacks that must be weighed in every sector where it is used, such as agriculture, industry, transport and weather monitoring.
sla_notes_details: Advantages: high speed and accuracy, consistent quality, ability to work continuously and in dangerous places, reduced labour cost in the long term, and safety. Disadvantages: high initial and maintenance cost, job losses for unskilled workers, dependence on electricity and technology, technical failures that can stop production, security risks such as hacking and need for skilled staff. Scenarios: in agriculture, automatic irrigation saves water; in industry, robots assemble products; in transport, automatic train signalling improves safety; in weather, automatic stations record data continuously. Learners discuss ethics and social effects and give recommendations.
sla_notes_illustrations: An automated irrigation system in a horticulture farm reduces water use by about a third and saves labour, but the farmer must invest in sensors and pay a technician for repairs.
sla_notes_daily_life: Banks use automatic teller machines to serve customers 24 hours a day but must protect them from fraud and power failure.
sla_exercise: State two advantages of automation in industry.::Increased speed and accuracy, and consistent product quality.||Give one disadvantage of automated systems.::High initial cost (or job losses or dependence on power).||How does automation benefit agriculture?::Automatic irrigation and monitoring save water and labour and improve yields.

sla_notes_intro: Learners design and build a simple automated system that solves a local problem, using a microcontroller, sensors and actuators or a simulator.
sla_notes_details: Steps: identify the problem (for example plants not watered, lights left on); state requirements; choose components (soil moisture sensor, microcontroller, relay, pump, power source); draw a block diagram and flowchart; write the program (read the sensor, if value is below the threshold switch the pump on else off, repeat); build the circuit or simulate in a virtual lab such as Tinkercad; test with different conditions; improve and document. Safety rules for electronic circuits are observed, such as correct polarity and not touching live wires.
sla_notes_illustrations: Pseudocode: loop forever, read moisture; if moisture is less than 30 then pump ON else pump OFF; wait 10 seconds. Testing with a dry and a wet soil sample confirms that the pump switches correctly.
sla_notes_daily_life: Such a system can be used in school gardens, in poultry houses to control temperature, or in homes to switch security lights automatically.
sla_exercise: Which component allows a microcontroller to switch a pump that uses higher power?::A relay (or transistor driver).||Why is a flowchart drawn before programming?::To plan the logic and the sequence of decisions of the system.||How can the system be tested?::By giving it different sensor conditions and checking that the actuator responds correctly.

sla_notes_intro: Emerging technologies are new or developing technologies that are expected to change the way people live and work. Their full effect is not yet realised.
sla_notes_details: Examples include artificial intelligence, machine learning, Internet of Things, blockchain, cloud and edge computing, big data, 5G, robotics and drones, 3D printing, holographic imaging and virtual and augmented reality (VR and AR). VR creates a fully simulated environment, while AR overlays digital information on the real world. Importance: solving complex problems, improving efficiency and creating new jobs and businesses. Advantages include convenience, better healthcare, education and productivity; disadvantages include privacy loss, job displacement, high cost, digital divide, security risks and environmental waste. Learners research one technology and present its meaning, types, importance and impact.
sla_notes_illustrations: In medical training a VR headset lets a student practise a surgical procedure safely; in shopping an AR app shows how furniture would look in a room.
sla_notes_daily_life: Mobile money, drones for delivering medicine and smart speakers are emerging technologies that have already entered daily life in Tanzania and elsewhere.
sla_exercise: Differentiate VR from AR.::VR replaces the real world with a simulated environment, while AR adds digital information to the real world.||Give two examples of emerging technologies.::Artificial intelligence and blockchain (or Internet of Things).||State one disadvantage of emerging technologies.::They can cause job displacement or threaten privacy.

sla_name: Building blocks of artificial intelligence
sla_assessment_criteria: Practical understanding of building blocks and components of artificial intelligence is correctly demonstrated.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the ability of machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence such as learning, reasoning and perception. Learners explore its components practically.
sla_notes_details: Basic AI algorithms include search algorithms (breadth first, depth first, A star), rule-based systems and logic (for example in Prolog), and decision trees. Machine learning lets computers learn from data: supervised learning uses labelled data (classification and regression), unsupervised learning finds patterns (clustering) and reinforcement learning learns through rewards. Neural networks are made of layers of artificial neurons; each neuron computes a weighted sum of inputs plus a bias and passes it through an activation function, and learning adjusts the weights by back propagation. Practical work uses Python libraries such as scikit-learn or online tools to train a model with training and testing data and evaluate accuracy.
sla_notes_illustrations: A classifier is trained on 100 labelled photos of maize leaves, healthy or diseased. When tested on 20 new photos it labels 18 correctly, so the accuracy is 90 percent.
sla_notes_daily_life: Voice assistants, spam filters, crop disease detection and translation apps such as Swahili translators use machine learning.
sla_exercise: Define machine learning.::A field of AI in which computers learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed.||Differentiate supervised from unsupervised learning.::Supervised learning uses labelled data, while unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabelled data.||What does each neuron in a neural network compute?::A weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias, passed through an activation function.

sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Emerging technologies affect health, education, business, agriculture, security and social life. Learners investigate and demonstrate these impacts practically.
sla_notes_details: Positive impacts: telemedicine and AI diagnostics in health, online and adaptive learning in education, mobile money and e-commerce in business, precision agriculture and drones for farming, smart cities and improved public services. Negative impacts: unemployment through automation, deepfakes and misinformation, cyber crime, addiction and health effects, energy use, e-waste and unequal access. Ethical issues include bias in AI, privacy, accountability and consent. Learners use surveys and demonstrations, for example testing an AI tool for translation or a VR application, then evaluate benefits and risks and propose responsible use policies.
sla_notes_illustrations: A class demonstrates a speech-to-text tool that produces notes from a lesson, then discusses its accuracy, privacy of recordings and how it may help learners with hearing difficulties.
sla_notes_daily_life: Farmers receive weather alerts by SMS, and patients in remote areas consult doctors by video, showing benefits in daily life.
sla_exercise: Give one positive impact of emerging technology in health.::Telemedicine allows patients in remote areas to consult specialists.||What is one ethical issue in AI?::Bias in the data or decisions (or privacy).||Suggest one way to use technology responsibly.::Protect personal data and verify information before sharing it.

sla_name: Advanced data analysis using appropriate tools
sla_assessment_criteria: An advanced data analysis using appropriate tools is correctly performed.
sla_teaching_aids: Internet resources|Computer system|Raw data|Analysis software (ChartGPT|Excell|SPSS|Etc)|NVDA|Braille devices
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Data analysis is the process of inspecting, cleaning, transforming and modelling data to discover useful information and support decisions. Learners use tools such as Excel and Python.
sla_notes_details: Steps: define the question, collect data (surveys, sensors, open data), clean it (remove duplicates, handle missing values, correct errors), explore it using descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, quartiles), and analyse using techniques such as sorting, filtering, pivot tables, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing. In Excel use formulas (AVERAGE, COUNTIF, VLOOKUP), pivot tables and the Data Analysis tool. In Python use the pandas library: read_csv to load, describe to summarise, groupby to aggregate and corr for correlation; NumPy for calculations. Results are interpreted in context and conclusions are stated with limits of the data.
sla_notes_illustrations: A CSV file of test scores is loaded with pandas; df.groupby('class')['score'].mean() shows the average for each class, and the correlation between study hours and score is 0.8, indicating a strong positive relationship.
sla_notes_daily_life: Businesses analyse sales data to decide what to stock, and health officers analyse clinic records to detect disease outbreaks.
sla_exercise: Name the first step in data analysis.::Defining the question or problem to be answered.||Which Python library is widely used for data analysis?::pandas.||What does a correlation of 0.8 suggest?::A strong positive relationship between the two variables.

sla_name: Visualising and interpreting data
sla_assessment_criteria: Appropriate skills to visualise and interpret data is correctly applied.
sla_references: TET(2023), COMPUTER SCIENCE SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Data visualisation presents data in graphs and charts so that patterns and trends can be understood quickly. Interpretation explains what the picture means.
sla_notes_details: Chart choice depends on the data: bar charts compare categories, line charts show trends over time, pie charts show parts of a whole, histograms show distribution, scatter plots show relationships and box plots show spread and outliers. Good visuals have a title, labelled axes with units, a legend, suitable scale and colours, and avoid misleading design. Tools are Excel charts, Python libraries matplotlib and seaborn, and dashboards such as Power BI or Google Data Studio. Interpretation identifies trends, outliers and relationships, states conclusions supported by the data, notes limitations and suggests actions.
sla_notes_illustrations: A line chart of monthly rainfall in Dodoma over one year shows a peak between December and April; interpretation states that most rain falls in these months, so planting should be timed accordingly.
sla_notes_daily_life: News and government reports use charts to show inflation, exam results and disease cases so citizens can understand them.
sla_exercise: Which chart is best for showing a trend over time?::A line chart.||Name two features of a good chart.::A title and labelled axes (or a legend).||What is an outlier?::A data value that is very different from the others.
